text: Given Essentials Threat credentials, when proofpoint_essentials_threat_get_messages_blocked is called with no time arguments, then the result covers the last hour and is shaped like proofpoint_tap_get_messages_blocked's result (queryEndTime, counts, capped lists).
steps: Obtain a real Proofpoint Essentials Threat API Integration Key/Secret for a test org (none available to DEV01)
Start the server locally and send tools/call proofpoint_essentials_threat_get_messages_blocked with X-Proofpoint-Essentials-Threat-Key / -Secret headers and no time arguments
Compare the response shape against proofpoint_tap_get_messages_blocked's documented shape
expect: 200 response with queryEndTime, a counts object, and capped event lists in the same shape as the TAP equivalent tool; no error key
notes: No real Essentials account available -- not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md 2.5. Covered instead by tests/test_api_client.py::test_essentials_threat_messages_blocked_shape against a mocked transport: the shaping code (shape_siem) is shared verbatim with the already-shipped TAP tools, so the only new surface is the auth/host plumbing, which the client-method tests cover separately. This manual case runs once a real account is available.

text: Given two concurrent requests carry two different orgs' Essentials Admin credentials, when both call proofpoint_essentials_list_domains at the same time, then each response contains only its own org's domains, and neither request's credentials appear in the other's logs or response.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/test_middleware.py::test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_essentials_credentials -> 1 passed. Two concurrent GatewayCredentialsMiddleware calls with essentials_user="org-a-admin" / "org-b-admin" (0.01s simulated work in between) each observe only their own value before and after the await point -- same per-request contextvar isolation mechanism already proven for TAP's principal field, extended to essentials_user.
